title: Completeness of pure codegeneracy word relations within the endpoint degrees
statement: Let $\Delta$ be the category of nonempty finite ordinals $[r]=\{0<\cdots<r\}$ and nondecreasing maps [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. For $r\geq0$ and $0\leq i\leq r$, let $\sigma_i^r:[r+1]\to[r]$ be the nondecreasing surjection identifying $i$ and $i+1$. Fix integers $0\leq b\leq a$. A codegeneracy word from $[a]$ to $[b]$ is a finite composable sequence of these maps, including the empty word when $a=b$; its value is their composite, with composition read right to left. If two codegeneracy words from $[a]$ to $[b]$ have equal values as maps of ordered sets, one can transform one word into the other by finitely many replacements of adjacent subwords, in either direction, using only the typed relations $$\sigma_j^r\circ\sigma_i^{r+1}=\sigma_i^r\circ\sigma_{j+1}^{r+1}\qquad(r\geq0,\ 0\leq i\leq j\leq r).$$ All words and all replacements in the transformation involve only ordinals with degrees between $b$ and $a$; no coface or mixed relation is used.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), pure-codegeneracy normal-form input to its omitted proof; the codegeneracy relation is Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (5).

proof.text: Put $k=a-b$. Each generator lowers degree by one, so a word has exactly $k$ factors and is encoded, from left to right, by $(u_0,\ldots,u_{k-1})$, with factor $\sigma_{u_p}^{b+p}$ and $0\leq u_p\leq b+p$. This uses the ordinal category of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. The empty list is the sole word for $k=0$. On an integer $x$, a generator is $\sigma_i^r(x)=x-\mathbf1_{x>i}$, directly from its defining ordered adjacent collapse.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), explicit agent-written proof of the pure-codegeneracy case of its omitted proof; relation from Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (5).

proof.text: For an adjacent pair $(j,i)$ with $i\leq j$, the left degree is some $r$ and $j\leq r$. Replace $(j,i)$ by $(i,j+1)$ using the stated relation. It is typed since $i\leq r$ and $j+1\leq r+1$. Both pair composites send $x$ to $x-\mathbf1_{x>i}-\mathbf1_{x>j+1}$: on the left the second subtraction occurs precisely when $x-\mathbf1_{x>i}>j$, equivalently $x>j+1$; on the right the second subtraction occurs precisely when $x-\mathbf1_{x>j+1}>i$, equivalently $x>i$. Thus replacement preserves the value, also after composition with the unchanged surrounding factors.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), explicit agent-written proof of the pure-codegeneracy case of its omitted proof; relation from Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (5).

proof.text: Define the nonnegative integer $D(u)=\sum_{p=0}^{k-1}(b+p-u_p)$. Each replacement in step 2 raises the sum of the indices by exactly one, and hence lowers $D$ by one. Induction on $D$ proves termination at an increasing list: if no adjacent pair satisfies $u_p\geq u_{p+1}$ we are done; otherwise do that replacement and apply the induction hypothesis to its smaller deficit. For $D=0$ every $u_p=b+p$, already strictly increasing. We have therefore constructed a finite allowed path from every word to a word $t_0<\cdots<t_{k-1}$ with the same value.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), explicit agent-written proof of the pure-codegeneracy case of its omitted proof; relation from Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (5).

proof.text: For an increasing word with index set $T$, its value satisfies $q(x)=x-\#\{t\in T:t<x\}$ for $0\leq x\leq a$. Prove this by induction on $k$, allowing all endpoints $b\leq a$. At $k=0$ it is the identity formula. For $k>0$ put $t=t_{k-1}$ and write $q=v\circ\sigma_t^{a-1}$, where $v$ is the increasing word from $[a-1]$ to $[b]$ with index set $T\setminus\{t\}$. If $x\leq t$, then $\sigma_t(x)=x$ and $t$ is not counted, giving the formula by induction. If $x>t$, then $\sigma_t(x)=x-1\geq t$ and all $k-1$ preceding indices are strictly below $t$, so induction gives $q(x)=(x-1)-(k-1)=x-k$, again the claimed formula.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), explicit agent-written proof of the pure-codegeneracy case of its omitted proof; relation from Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (5).

proof.text: For $0\leq x<a$, the formula in step 4 gives $q(x+1)-q(x)=1-\mathbf1_{x\in T}$. Indeed, among distinct integer indices, the counts for $t<x+1$ and $t<x$ differ by one exactly when $x\in T$. Consequently $T=\{x\in\{0,\ldots,a-1\}:q(x)=q(x+1)\}$. Thus equal values of two increasing words give the same index set; listing that finite set in strictly increasing order gives the same list (successively take the least remaining element), hence the identical typed word.

source.place: Tag 0168 (lemma-face-degeneracy-category), explicit agent-written proof of the pure-codegeneracy case of its omitted proof; relation from Tag 0167 (lemma-relations-face-degeneracy), part (5).

proof.text: Given the original two words with equal values, apply step 3 to obtain increasing words. Their values remain equal by step 2, so step 5 identifies them. Concatenate the first finite replacement path with the reverse of the second. At every replacement the sequence of factor degrees remains $b,b+1,\ldots,a-1$ from left to right, so all intermediate ordinals have degrees between $b$ and $a$. Each move is precisely one of the given codegeneracy relations in an unchanged word context; the reverse moves are allowed by the statement. For $a=b$ both paths are empty. This proves every clause.
